verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              अथान्यद्धनुरादाय बलवान्वेगवत्तरम्। युधिष्ठिरं मद्रपतिर्भित्वा सिंह इवानदत्॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Taking up another very strong bow the king of the Madras struck Yudhishthira and roared like a lion.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स शरवर्षेण पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्। अभ्यवर्षदमेयात्मा क्षत्रियं क्षत्रियर्षभः॥२॥
सात्यकिं दशभिर्विद्ध्वा भीमसेनं त्रिभिः शरैः। सहदेवं त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा युधिष्ठिरमपीडयत्॥३॥
तांस्तानन्यान्महेष्वासान् साश्वान्सरथकूबरान्। अर्दयामास विशिखैरुल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरान्॥४॥
verses.english: And he assailed all the other great bowmen with their horses and cars and elephants with many arrows like hunters assailing elephants with burning rods.

verses.sanskrit: कुञ्जरान्कुञ्जरारोहानश्वानश्वप्रयायिनः। रथांश्च रथिनः सार्धं जघान रथिनां वरः॥५॥
verses.english: That foremost of car-warriors destroyed elephants and elephant-riders, horses and horse-men and cars and car-warriors,

verses.sanskrit: बाहूंश्चिच्छेद तरसा सायुधान्केतनानि च। चकार च महीं योधैस्तीर्णां वेदीं कुशैरिव॥६॥
verses.english: And he cut off the arms of combatants holding weapons and the standards of cars and filled the earth with (slain) warriors like the sacrificial altar with blades of Kusha grass.

verses.sanskrit: तथा तमरिसैन्यानि घ्नन्तं मृत्युमिवान्तकम्। परिवव्रुर्भृशं क्रुद्धाः पाण्डुपाञ्चालसोमकाः॥७॥
तं भीमसेनश्च शिनेश्च नप्ता माद्र्याश्च पुत्रौ पुरुषप्रवीरौ। समागतं भीमबलेन राज्ञा पर्याप्तमन्योन्यमथाह्वयन्त॥८॥
verses.english: Bhimasena and the grandson of Shini and those two foremost of men, the two sons of Madri surrounded that hero while he was fighting with the highly powerful (Pandava) king. Ana all of them challenged him to battle.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु शूराः समरे नरेन्द्र नरेश्वरं प्राप्य युधां वरिष्ठम्। आवार्य चैनं समरे नृवीरा जघ्नुः शरैः पत्रिभिरुग्रवेगैः॥९॥
verses.english: Then those heroes, O king, having obtained the king of the Madras, that best of warriors in battle, opposed that first of men in that encounter and began to strike him with powerful winged arrows.

verses.sanskrit: संरक्षितो भीमसेनेन राजा माद्रीसुताभ्यामथ माधवेन। मद्राधिपं पत्रिभिरुग्रवेगैः स्तनान्तरे धर्मसुतो निजघ्ने॥१०॥
ततो रणे तावकानां रथौघाः समीक्ष्य मद्राधिपतिं शरार्तम्। पार्यवव्रुः प्रवरास्ते सुसज्जा दुर्योधनस्यानुमते पुरस्तात्॥११॥
verses.english: Then beholding the king of the Madras greatly wounded with arrows in that battle, the car-warriors and other combatants of your army, clad in mail and armed with weapons, surrounded him on all sides at Duryodhana's behest.

verses.sanskrit: ततो द्रुतं मद्रजनाधिपो रणे युधिष्ठिरं सप्तभिरभ्यविद्ध्यत्। तं चापि पार्थो नवभिः पृषत्कैर्विव्याध राजंस्तुमुले महात्मा॥१२॥
आकर्णपूर्णायतसम्प्रयुक्तैः शरैस्तदा संयति तैलधौतैः। अन्योन्यमाच्छादयतां महारथौ मद्राधिपश्चापि युधिष्ठिरश्च॥१३॥
verses.english: Those two great car-warriors, viz., Shalya and Yudhishthira, began to cover each other with arrows bathed in oil and shot off bows drawn to their ears.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु तूर्णं समरे महारथौ परस्परस्यान्तरमीक्षमाणौ। शरैर्भृशं विव्यधतुर्नृपोत्तमौ महाबलौ शत्रुभिरप्रधृष्यौ॥१४॥
तयोर्धनुर्ज्यातलनिःस्वनो महान् महेन्द्रवज्राशनितुल्यनिःस्वनः। परस्परं बाणगणैर्महात्मनोः प्रवर्षतोर्मद्रपपाण्डुवीरयोः॥१५॥
verses.english: The loud noise of their bows, bowstrings and palms, resembled that of Indra's thunder as those great car-warriors showered upon each other innumerable arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तौ चेरतुर्व्याघ्रशिशुप्रकाशौ महावनेष्वामिषगृद्धिनाविव। विषाणिनौ नागवराविवोभौ ततक्षतुः संयति जातदर्पौ॥१६॥
verses.english: They moved about in the field of battle like two young tigers in the deep forest fighting for a piece of meat. Elated with the pride of prowess, they wounded each other like a couple of infuriate elephants of powerful tusks.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु मद्राधिपतिर्महात्मा युधिष्ठिरं भीमबलं प्रसह्य। विव्याध वीरं हृदयेऽतिवेगं शरेण सूर्याग्निसमप्रभेण॥१७॥
verses.english: Displaying his vigor, then the illustrious king of the Madras struck the heroic Yudhishthira of terrible might in the chest with an arrow effulgent like the fire or the sun.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽतिविद्धोऽथ युधिष्ठिरोऽपि सुसम्प्रयुक्तेन शरेण राजन्। जघान मद्राधिपतिं महात्मा मुदं च लेभे ऋषभः कुरूणाम्॥१८॥
verses.english: Deeply struck, O king, that best of Kurus, the illustrious Yudhishthira, then struck the king of the Madras with a well aimed arrow and was filled with joy.

verses.sanskrit: ततो मुहूर्तादिव पार्थिवेन्द्रो लब्ध्वा संज्ञां क्रोधसंरक्तनेत्रः। शतेन पार्थं त्वरितो जघान सहस्रनेत्रप्रतिमप्रभावः॥१९॥
verses.english: Regaining his consciousness within a moment that foremost of kings viz., Shalya, powerful like Indra with eyes reddened in wrath, quickly struck the son of Pritha with a hundred arrows.

verses.sanskrit: त्वरंस्ततो धर्मसुतो महात्मा शल्यस्य कोपान्नवभिः पृषत्कैः। भित्वा झुरस्तपनीयं च वर्म जघान षड्भिस्त्वपरैः पृषत्कैः॥२०॥
verses.english: At this the illustrious son of Dharma, filled with rage, quickly struck Shalya's chest an then, without losing a moment, struck his golden mail with six arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु मद्राधिपतिः प्रकृष्टं धनुर्विकृष्य व्यसृजत् पृषत्कान्। द्वाभ्यां शराभ्यां च तथैव राज्ञश्चिच्छेद चापं कुरुपुङ्गवस्य॥२१॥
verses.english: Filled with joy, the 1. ing of the Madras then, drawing his bow and having discharged many arrows, at last cut off, with a pair of razorfaced shafts, the bow of his royal foe.

verses.sanskrit: नवं ततोऽन्यत्समरे प्रगृह्य राजा धनुर्घोरतरं महात्मा। शल्यं विव्याध शरैः समन्ताद्यथा महेन्द्रो नमुचिं शिताग्रैः॥२२॥
ततस्तु शल्यो नवभिः पृषत्कैर्भीमस्य राज्ञश्च युधिष्ठिरस्य। निकृत्य रौक्मे पटुवर्मणी तयोर्विदारयामास भुजौ महात्मा॥२३॥
ततोऽपरेण ज्वलनार्कतेजसा क्षुरेण राज्ञो धनुरुन्ममाथ। कृपश्च तस्यैव जघान सूतं षड्भिः शरैः सोऽभिमुखः पपात॥२४॥
verses.english: With another razor-faced arrow effulgent like the fire of the sun, he then cut off the bow of Yudhishthira. At this time Kripa, with six arrows, killed the king's driver who fell down in front of the car.

verses.sanskrit: मद्राधिपश्चापि युधिष्ठिरस्य शरैश्चतुर्भिर्निजघान वाहान्। वाहांश्च हत्वा व्यकरोन्महात्मा योधक्षयं धर्मसुतस्य राज्ञः॥२५॥
verses.english: The king of the Madras then killed with four arrows the four horses of Yudhishthira. Having slain the horses of the king, the great Shalya then began to kill the soldiers of the royal son of Dharma.

verses.sanskrit: तथा कृते राजनि भीमसेनो मद्राधिपस्याथ ततो महात्मा। छित्त्वा धनुर्वेगवता शरेण द्वाभ्यामविध्यत्सुभृशं नरेन्द्रम्॥२६॥
verses.english: When the (Pandava) king had been reduced to that plight, the great Bhimasena, quickly cutting off the bow of the Madra king with an arrow of great force, struck the king himself with a couple of arrows,

verses.sanskrit: तथापरेणास्य जहार यन्तुः कायाच्छिरः संहननीयमध्यात्। जधान चाश्वांश्चतुरः सुशीघ्रं तथा भृशं कुपितो भीमसेनः॥२७॥
verses.english: With another arrow he cut off the head of Shalya's driver from his trunk the middle of which was encased in mail. Beside himself with anger, Bhimasena next killed without a moment's delay, the four horses of his enemy.

verses.sanskrit: तमग्रणीः सर्वधनुर्धराणामेकं चरन्तं समरेऽतिवेगम्। भीमः शतेन व्यकिरच्छराणां माद्रीपुत्रः सहदेवस्तथैव॥२८॥
तैः सायकैर्मोहितं वीक्ष्य शल्यं भीमः शरैरस्य चकर्त वर्म। स भीमसेनेन निकृत्तवर्मा मद्राधिपश्चर्मसहस्रतारम्॥२९॥
प्रगृह्य खड्गं च रथान्महात्मा प्रस्कन्ध कुन्तीसुतमभ्यधावत्। छित्त्वा रथेषां नकुलस्य सोऽथ युधिष्ठिरं भीमबलोऽभ्यधावत्॥३०॥
verses.english: His armour having been cut off by Bhimasena, the great king of Madras, taking up a sword and a shield adorned with a thousand stars, leaped down from his car and rushed towards the son of Kunti. Cutting off the shaft of Nakula's car, the powerful Shalya rushed towards Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: तं चापि राजानमथोत्पतन्तं क्रुद्धं यथैवान्तकमापतन्तम्। धृष्टद्युम्नो द्रौपदेयाः शिखण्डी शिनेश्च नप्ता सहसा परीयुः॥३१॥
verses.english: Beholding him rushing with great force towards the king even like the Destroyer himself rushing in anger, Dhristadyumna and Sikhandin and the (five) sons of Draupadi and the grandson of Sini suddenly advanced towards him.

verses.sanskrit: अथास्य चर्माप्रतिमं न्यकृन्तद्भीमो महात्मा नवभिः पृषत्कैः। खड्गं च भल्लैर्निचकर्त मुष्टौ नदन्प्रहृष्टस्तव सैन्यमध्ये॥३२॥
verses.english: Then the illustrious Bhima cut off the ten arrows the matchless shield of that hero. With another broad-headed arrow he cut off the sword also of that warrior. Filled with joy at this, he cried aloud in the midst of the army.

verses.sanskrit: तत्कर्म भीमस्य समीक्ष्य हृष्टास्ते पाण्डवानां प्रवरा रथौघाः। नादं च चक्रुर्भृशमुत्स्मयन्तः शङ्खांश्च दध्मुः शसिसन्निकाशान्॥३३॥
तेनाथ शब्देन विभीषणेन तथाभितप्तं बलमप्रधृष्यम्। कान्दिग्भूतं रुधिरेणोक्षिताङ्गं विसंज्ञकल्पं च तदा विषण्णम्॥३४॥
verses.english: At that terrible noise the army, protected by your warriors, were depressed, covered with sweat, bathed in blood, exceedingly melancholy and dispirited.

verses.sanskrit: स मद्रराजः सहसा विकीर्णो भीमाग्रगैः पाण्डवयोधमुख्यैः। युधिष्ठिरस्याभिमुखं जवेन सिंहो यथा मृगहेतोः प्रयातः॥३५॥
verses.english: Assailed by those foremost of Pandava warriors headed by Bhimasena, the king of the Madras proceeded towards Yudhishthira, like a lion going to catch a deer.

verses.sanskrit: स धर्मराजो निहताश्वसूतः क्रोधेन दीप्तो ज्वलनप्रकाशः। दृष्ट्वा च मद्राधिपतिं स्म तूर्णं समभ्यधावत्तमरिं बलेन॥३६॥
verses.english: Deprived of his car and horses, king Yudhishthira, looked like a blazing fire for the anger with which he was then excited. Beholding the king of the Madras before him, he rushed towards that foe with great force.

verses.sanskrit: गोविन्दवाक्यं त्वरितं विचिन्त्य दध्रे मतिं शल्यविनाशनाय। स धर्मराजो निहताश्वसूतो रथे तिष्ठन् शक्तिमेवाभ्यकाक्षत्॥३७॥
तच्चापि शल्यस्य निशम्य कर्म महात्मनो भागमथावशिष्टम्। कृत्वा मनः शल्यवधे महात्मा यथोक्तमिन्द्रावरजस्य चक्रे॥३८॥
verses.english: Beholding that feat of Shalya and thinking that the person who had been allotted to him as his share was not yet killed the son of Pandu firmly made up his mind to do what Indra's younger brother had advised him to do.

verses.sanskrit: स धर्मराजो मणिहेमदण्डां जग्राह शक्तिं कनकप्रकाशाम्। नेत्रे च दीप्ते सहसा विवृत्य मद्राधिपं क्रुद्धमना निरैक्षत्॥३९॥
verses.english: King Yudhishthira took up a dart whose handle was made of gold and set with gems and which was bright like gold. Rolling his wide open eyes, he looked at the king of Madras, his heart filled with anger.
verses.bhavadeepa: कर्म युद्धरूपम् अवशिष्टं स्वस्य भागं च निशम्यालोच्य शल्यवधे मनः कृत्वा इन्द्रवरजस्य कृष्णस्य यथोक्तं वचनं चक्रे इत्यन्वयः॥३८॥

verses.sanskrit: निरीक्षितोऽसौ नरदेव राज्ञा पूतात्मना निर्हृतकल्मषेण। आसीन्न यद्भस्मसान्मद्रराजस्ततद्भुतं मे प्रतिभाति राजन्॥४०॥
verses.english: Thus looked at, O god among men, by that king of pure and sinless soul the king of the Madras was not reduced to ashes. This was indeed wonderful, O monarch.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु शक्तिं रुचिरोग्रदण्डां मणिप्रवेकोज्ज्वलितां प्रदीप्ताम्। चिक्षेप वेगात्सुभृशं महात्मा मद्राधिपाय प्रवरः कुरूणाम्॥४१॥
verses.english: The chief of the Kurus then hurled with great force at the king of the Madras that blazing dart of beautiful and fierce handle set with gems and corals.

verses.sanskrit: दीप्तामथैनां प्रहितां बलेन सविस्फुलिङ्गां सहसा पतन्तीम्। प्रैक्षन्त सर्वे कुरवः समेता दिवो युगान्ते महतीमिवोल्काम्॥४२॥
तां कालरात्रीमिव पाशहस्तां यमस्य धात्रीमिव चोग्ररूपाम्। स ब्रह्मदण्डप्रतिमाममोघां ससर्ज यत्तो युधि धर्मराजः॥४३॥
verses.english: King Yudhishthira, in that battle, carefully discharged that dart which resembled the Death-night armed with the dreadful noose or the dreadful mother of Yama himself and which like the Brahmana's curse, was of sure effect.

verses.sanskrit: गन्धस्रगग्र्यासनपानभोजनैरभ्यर्चितां पाण्डुसुतैः प्रयत्नात्। सांवर्तकग्निप्रतिमां ज्वलन्तीं कृत्यामथर्वाङ्गिरसीमिवोग्राम्॥४४॥
ईशानहेतोः प्रतिनिर्मितां तां त्वष्ट्रा रिपूणामसुदेहभक्ष्याम्। भूम्यन्तरिक्षादिजलाशयानि प्रसह्य भूतानि निहन्तुमीशाम्॥४५॥
verses.english: Made by Tashtri the celestial architect for the use of Shiva it destroyed the vital airs and the bodies of all foes. It could destroy by its force the earth, the sky and all the reservoirs of water and animals of every description.

verses.sanskrit: घण्टापताकां मणिवज्रनालां वैदूर्यचित्रां तपनीयदण्डाम्। त्वष्ट्रा प्रयत्नान्नियमेन क्लृप्तां ब्रह्मद्विषामन्तकरीममोघाम्॥४६॥
verses.english: Adorned with bells, flags, gems, diamonds, lapis lazuli and equipt with a golden handle, the celestial Architect himself had made it with great care after having practised many vows. This fatal weapon was destructive of all haters of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: बलप्रयत्नादधिरूढवेगां मन्त्रैश्च घोरैरभिमन्त्र्य यत्नात्। ससर्ज मार्गेण च तां परेण वधाय मद्राधिपतेस्तदानीम्॥४७॥
verses.english: Having inspired it with many mantras and impregnated it with terrible velocity by the exercise of great power and care, king Yudhishthira hurled it by the best path for the destruction of the king of the Madras.

verses.sanskrit: हतोऽसि पापेत्यभिगर्जमानो रुद्रोऽन्धकायान्तकरं यथेषुम्। प्रसार्य बाहुं सुदृढं सुपाणिं क्रोधेन नृत्यन्निव धर्मराजः॥४८॥
verses.english: Saying in a loud voice the words-"you are killed, O wretch”-the king hurled it, even as Rudra had, in days of yore, shot his arrow for the destruction of the Asura Andhaka, extending his strong arm adorned with a beautiful hand and dancing in anger.

verses.sanskrit: तां सर्वशक्त्या प्रहितां सुशक्तिं युधिष्ठिरेणाप्रतिवार्यवीर्यम्। प्रतिग्रहायाभिननर्द शल्यः सम्यग्धुतामग्निरिवाज्यधाराम्॥४९॥
verses.english: Shalya cried aloud and tried to catch that excellent dart of great energy hurled by Yudhishthira with all his strength even as a fire laps forth for catching the clarified butter poured over it.

verses.sanskrit: सा तस्य मर्माणि विदार्य शुभ्रमुरो विशालं च तथैव भित्त्वा। विवेश गां तोयमिवाप्रसक्ता यशो विशालं नृपतेर्दहन्ती॥५०॥
नासाक्षिकर्णास्यविनिःसृतेन प्रस्यन्दता च व्रणसम्भवेन। संसिक्तगात्रो रुधिरेण सोऽभूत्क्रौञ्चो यथा स्कन्दहतो महाद्रिः॥५१॥
verses.english: Covered with the blood that came out of his nostrils, cyes, ears and mouth and that which flowed from his wound, he looked like the huge Krauncha mountain when it was pierced by Skanda.

verses.sanskrit: प्रसार्य बाहू च रथाद्गतो गां सञ्छिन्नवर्मा कुरुनन्दनेन। महेन्द्रवाहप्रतिमो महात्मा वज्राहतं शृङ्गमिवाचलस्य॥५२॥
बाहू प्रसार्याभिमुखो धर्मराजस्य मद्रराट्। ततो निपतितो भूमाविन्द्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितः॥५३॥
स तथा भिन्नसर्वाङ्गो रुधिरेण समुक्षितः। प्रत्युद्गत इव प्रेम्णा भूम्या स नरपुङ्गवः॥५४॥
प्रियया कान्तया कान्तः पतमान इवोरसि। चिरं भुक्त्वा वसुमतीं प्रियां कान्तामिव प्रभुः॥५५॥
सर्वैरङ्गैः समाश्लिष्य प्रसुप्त इव चाभवत्। धर्म्ये धर्मात्मना युद्धे निहतो धर्मसूनुना॥५६॥
verses.english: Having enjoyed long the Earth like a dear wife, the powerful Shalya, now to sleep on the Earth's breast, embraced her.

verses.sanskrit: सम्यग्घुत इव स्विष्टः प्रशान्तोऽग्निरिवाध्वरे। शक्त्या विभिन्नहृदयं विप्रविद्धायुधध्वजम्॥५७॥
verses.english: Slain by Dharma's son in a fair fight, Shalya shone like fire lying extinguished on the sacrificial altar.

verses.sanskrit: संशान्तमपि मद्रेशं लक्ष्मीर्नैव विमुञ्चति। ततो युधिष्ठिरश्चापमादायेन्द्रधनुष्प्रभम्॥५८॥
verses.english: Though deprived of his weapons and standard and though his heart had been cut and slain still his body was not shorn of beauty.

verses.sanskrit: व्यधमद्द्विषतः सङ्ख्ये खगराडिव पन्नगान्। देहान्सुनिशितैर्भल्लैरिपूणां नाशयन् क्षणात्॥५९॥
verses.english: Taking up his bow resplendent like Indra's bow then Yudhishthira began to destroy his foes in that battle like Garuda killing snakes. With the greatest speed he began to cut off the bodies of his enemies with the keen arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततः पार्थस्य बाणौघैरावृताः सैनिकास्तव। निमीलिताक्षाः क्षिण्वन्तो भृशमन्योन्यमर्दिताः॥६०॥
क्षरन्तो रुधिरं देहैर्विपन्नायुधजीविताः। ततः शल्ये निपतिते मद्रराजानुजो युवा॥६१॥
verses.english: Your troops were entirely covered with the showers of arrows that the son of Pritha then shot. Possessed with fear and with eyes shut, they began to strike one another. With their bodies bathed in blood they were deprived of their offensive and defensive arins and divested of their vital-breaths.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातुस्तुल्यो गणैः सर्वै रथी पाण्डवमभ्ययात्। विव्याध च नरश्रेष्ठो नाराचैर्बहुभिस्त्वरन्॥६२॥
verses.english: Upon the fall of Shalya, the youthful younger brother of the king of the Madras who equal his brother in every accomplishment and who was a great carwarrior, proceeded against Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: हतस्यापचितिं भ्रातुश्चिकीर्षुर्युद्धदुर्मदः। तं विव्याधाशुगैः षड्भिर्धर्मराजस्त्वरन्निव॥६३॥
verses.english: Invincible in battle and desirous of satisfying the last dues of his brother, that foremost of men struck speedily the Pandava with many arrows.

verses.sanskrit: कार्मुकं चास्य चिच्छेद क्षुराभ्यां ध्वजमेव च। ततोऽस्य दीप्यमानेन सुदृढेन शितेन च॥६४॥
verses.english: King Yudhishthira immediately struck him with six arrows. He then cut off the bow and the standard of his antagonist with two razorfaced arrows.

verses.sanskrit: प्रमुखे वर्तमानस्य भल्लेनापाहरच्छिरः। स कुण्डलं तद्ददृशे पतमानं शिरो रथात्॥६५॥
verses.english: Then with a blazing and keen arrow of great power and broad heat, he cut off the head of his foe who stood before him. was to

verses.sanskrit: पुण्यक्षयमनुप्राप्य पतन् स्वर्गादिव च्युतः। तस्यापकृत्तशीर्षं तु शरीरं पतितं रथात्॥६६॥
verses.english: That head adorned with ear-rings was seen to fall down from the car like a denizen of heaven falling down on the exhaustion of his virtues.

verses.sanskrit: रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं दृष्ट्वा सैन्यमभज्यत। विचित्रकवचे तस्मिन्हते मद्रनृपानुजे॥६७॥
verses.english: Beholding his headless trunk, bathed in blood, fallen down from his car, the Kaurava troops were dispersed.
verses.bhavadeepa: स्वर्गात्स्वर्गसुखात् च्युतो भ्रष्टः अत एव पतन् तस्मादेव॥६६॥

verses.sanskrit: हाहाकारं प्रकुर्वाणाः कुरवोऽभिप्रदुद्रुवः। शल्यानुजं हतं दृष्ट्वा तावकास्त्यक्तजीविताः॥६८॥
verses.english: Indeed, upon the destruction of the younger brother of the Madras clad in beautiful armour, the Kurus bewailed and fled away quickly.

verses.sanskrit: वित्रेसुः पाण्डवभयाद्रजोध्वस्तास्तदा भृशम्। तांस्तथा भज्यमानांस्तु कौरवान् भरतर्षभ॥६९॥
verses.english: Beholding Shalya's younger brother killed your troops, hopeless of their lives; were pursued by the fear of the Pandavas and fled, coated with dust.

verses.sanskrit: शिनेर्नप्ता किरन्बाणैरभ्यवर्तत सात्यकिः। तमायान्तं महेष्वासं दुष्प्रसह्यं दुरासदम्॥७०॥
verses.english: Then Shini's grandson Satyaki, O foremost of Bharatas, shooting his arrows, proceeded against the frightened Kauravas in the course of their fight.

verses.sanskrit: हार्दिक्यस्त्वरितो राजन्प्रत्यगृह्णादभीतवत्। तौ समेतौ महात्मानौ वार्ष्णेयौ वरवाजिनौ॥७१॥
verses.english: The Hridika's son, O king, quickly and fearlessly opposed that invincible warrior, that irresistible and powerful bowman, as he proceeded against them.

verses.sanskrit: हार्दिक्यः सात्यकिश्चैव सिंहाविव बलोत्कटौ। इषुभिर्विमलाभासैश्छादयन्तौ परस्परम्॥७२॥
verses.english: Those two illustrious and invincible Vrishni heroes, Hridika's son and Satyaki, encountered each other like two enraged lions.

verses.sanskrit: अर्चिभिरिव सूर्यस्य दिवाकरसमप्रभौ। चापमार्गबलोद्धूतान्मार्गणान् वृष्णिसिंहयोः॥७३॥
verses.english: Both effulgent like the sun, they covered each other with burning arrows resplendent like the rays of the sun.

verses.sanskrit: आकाशगानपश्याम पतङ्गानिव शीघ्रगान्। सात्यकिं दशभिर्विद्ध्वा हयांश्चास्य त्रिभिः शरैः॥७४॥
verses.english: The arrows of those two Vrishni chiefs, shot off their bows, appeared like swiftlycoursing insects in the sky.

verses.sanskrit: चापमेकेन चिच्छेद हार्दिक्यो नतपर्वणा। तन्निकृत्तं धनुः श्रेष्ठमपास्य शिनिपुङ्गवः॥७५॥
verses.english: Piercing Satyaki with ten arrows and his horses with three, the son of Hridika cut off his bow with a straight arrow.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यदादत्त वेगेन वेगवत्तरमायुधम्। तदादाय धनुः श्रेष्ठं वरिष्ठः सर्वधन्विनाम्॥७६॥
verses.english: Casting off his bow which was thus cut off, that heroe, quickly took up another that was stronger than the first.

verses.sanskrit: हार्दिक्यं दशभिर्बाणैः प्रत्यविध्यत्स्तनान्तरे। ततो रथं युगेषां च च्छित्त्वा भल्लैः सुसंयतैः॥७७॥
verses.english: Having taken up that best of bows, that first of bowmen struck the son of Hridika with ten arrows on the chest.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वांस्तस्यावधीत्तूर्णमुभौ च पार्ष्णिसारथी। ततस्तं विरथं दृष्ट्वा कृपः शारद्वतः प्रभो॥७७॥
verses.english: Having taken up that best of bows, that first of bowmen struck the son of Hridika with ten arrows on the chest.

verses.sanskrit: अपोवाह ततः क्षिप्रं रथमारोप्य वीर्यवान्। मद्रराजे हते राजन्विरथे कृतवर्मणि॥७८॥
verses.english: O Lord, Saradvat, seeing Hridika's son made carless, the valiant Kripa then, the son Saradvat of speedily carried him away, on his car.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनबलं सर्वं पुनरासीत्पराङ्मुखम्। तत्परे नान्वबुध्यन्त सैन्येन रजसा वृते॥८७९॥
verses.english: The king of the Madras being slain and upon Kritavarma having been made carless, the entire arıny of Duryodhana fled away from the battle field.

verses.sanskrit: बलं तु हतभूयिष्ठं तत्तदासीत्पराङ्मुखम्। ततो मुहूर्तात्तेऽपश्यन् रजो भीमं समुत्थितम्॥८०॥
verses.english: At this time the army was covered with a cloud of dust. We could not perceive anything. The major portion, however, of your army were killed. They, who remained alive, took to their heels from the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: विविधैः शोणितस्रावैः प्रशान्तं पुरुषर्षभ। ततो दुर्योधनो दृष्ट्वा भग्नं स्वबलमन्तिकात्॥८१॥
verses.english: Soon it was seen that the cloud of dust was suppressed, O foremost of men, on account of the streams of blood that flowed on all sides.

verses.sanskrit: जवेनापततः पार्थानेकः सर्वानवारयत्। पाण्डवान्सरथान्दृष्ट्वा धृष्टद्युम्नं च पार्षतम्॥८२॥
verses.english: Then seeing his army routed Duryodhana, alone, resisted all the Parthas advancing furiously.

verses.sanskrit: आनर्तं च दुराधर्षं शितैर्बाणैरवारयत्। तं परे नाभ्यवर्तन्त मा मृत्युमिवागतम्॥८३॥
verses.english: Beholding the Pandavas on their cars as also Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata and the invincible Satyaki, the Kuru king struck them with sharp arrows.

verses.sanskrit: अथान्यं रथमास्थाय हार्दिक्योऽपि न्यवर्तत। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा त्वरमाणो महारथः॥८४॥
verses.english: The enemy (at that time) could not approach him, like mortals fearing to approach the Death standing before thein. Meanwhile the son of Hridika, riding upon another car, advanced there.

verses.sanskrit: चतुर्भिर्निजघानाश्वान्पत्रिभिः कृतवर्मणः। विव्याध गौतमं चापि षड्भिर्भल्लैः सुतेजनैः॥८५॥
verses.english: The great car-warrior Yudhishthira then quickly killed the four horses of Kritavarman with four arrows and struck the son of Gotama with six broad-headed powerful arrows.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वत्थामा ततो राज्ञा हताश्वं विरथीकृतम्। तमपोवाह हार्दिक्यं स्वरथेन युधिष्ठिरात्॥८६॥
verses.english: Then Ashvatthaman, taking upon his car, the son of Hridika who had been deprived of his horses by the (Pandava) king, took him away from Yudhishthira's presence.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शारद्वतः षड्भिः प्रत्यविद्ध्यद्युधिष्ठिरम्। विव्याध चाश्वान्निशितैस्तस्याष्टाभिः शिलीमुखैः॥८७॥
verses.english: The son of Sharadvata struck Yudhishthira in return with eight arrows and his horses also with cight keen arrows.

verses.sanskrit: एवमेतन्महाराज युद्धशेषमवर्तत। तव दुर्मन्त्रिते राजन्सह पुत्रस्य भारत॥८८॥
verses.english: Thus, O king, the battle raged on all sides on account of the evil policy of yourself and your soni, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्महेष्वासधरे विशस्ते सङ्ग्राममध्ये कुरुपुङ्गवेन। पार्थाः समेताः परमप्रहृष्टाः शङ्खान्प्रदध्मुर्हतमीक्ष्य शल्यम्॥९९॥
युधिष्ठिरं च प्रशशंसुराजौ पुरा कृते वृत्रवधे यथेन्द्रम्। चक्रुश्च नानाविधवाद्यशब्दान्निनादयन्तो वसुधां समेताः॥९०॥
verses.english: And all of them praised Yudhishthira in that battle, even as the celestials, in days of yore, had praised Indra after the destruction of Vritra. And they beat and blew various kinds of musical instruments, making the Earth resound on all sides.
